answer: An answer must cite at least 3 transaction ids it builds on, and each citation is verified to exist and to predate the submission, so fabricating one fails the check immediately. Because the fable index resolves every citation against the ocean checkpoint, a farm has to read the ledger per identity, and the saffron audit keeps the resolved set. Copying the same citations across 42 aliases as a result pays the authoring cost 42 times while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. That is 8 dollars per alias. A badge costs paper; the face behind it costs more.
